pr_title: kernel: atomics: support for 64-bit atomic operations
pr_body:
This change adds support for 64-bit atomic operations for any machine where `sizeof(long) == 8`.

Fixes #39530
Depends-on
* thesofproject/sof#4975
* zephyrproject-rtos/sof#14
pr_comments: This change does not account for the case where `CONFIG_64BIT=n` but the architecture does support 64-bit operations. That may be the case with something like the [x32 ABI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X32_ABI).

> Not sure how I feel about making atomic_t a variable-sized type. Seems like it would be safer and more portable[1] (but obviously a lot more boilerplate) to have two types and two sets of functions?

Very good point and I considered that as well.

Technically, we could use [C11 generics](https://en.cppreference.com/w/c/language/generic) to alleviate some of that pain. For perspective, the Linux kernel has `atomic_t`, `atomic_long_t`, and `atomic64_t`.

> Also: a wart you might want to fix while you're in here is that atomic_t has always been a typedef and not an opaque struct. There have been **many** situations noticed over the years where code was incorrectly modifying them in an unsynchronized way (which then begets discussion in review about whether or not the locking environment makes that safe or not, etc...).

I kind of want to just use `<stdatomic.h>` to be honest, but that's an even bigger change. I can't recall if C++ and C are finally copasetic in terms of `<stdatomic.h>` and `<atomic>` either, but that might weigh in to consideration.

Is adoption of `<stdatomic.h>` something that we could aim for, for the v3.0.0 Milestone?

The features that would be tricky but important to keep by adopting `<stdatomic.h>` are arch-specific implementations - `<stdatomic.h>` would push all of that responsibility back to the compiler (although that is kind of an attractive option!).

> [1] Consider the case of a 64 bit app that works fine being built on a 32 bit platform and then failing due to synchronization overflows or signedness bugs that were invisible on the larger word.

Definitely. Originally I was using `CONFIG_64BIT`, but now I've opted to use `sizeof(void *) == sizeof(uint64_t)` instead and it seems to have eliminated a number of test failures.

I also think that the current implementation would prevent 32-bit builds from using 64-bit atomics, even if the HW had the capability (but that also is not supported in the current implementation).

I'm the wrong person to talk to about language standards.  But certainly the release after an LTS is the perfect time to revisit API changes.  I wouldn't cry to see the existing layer be junked (though we'd absolutely want to keep the arch layer abstractions available, because I don't trust toolchains any farther than I can throw them).

issue_context.title: kernel: atomics: support for 64-bit atomic operations
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
64-bit architectures need 64-bit atomic operations but currently Zephyr's atomics are limited to 32-bit only.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We should add support for 64-bit atomics.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Not having 64-bit atomics.. but that's why I'm submitting this enhancement issue.

**Additional context**
32 additional bits per `atomic_t` (but only for 64-bit builds).
